paragraphs.title: The Destruction of the Regional Cities and the Lord’s Claim
paragraphs.paragraph: The prophecy describes the downfall of Tyre, Sidon, and the Philistine cities. Their wealth, fortifications, and pride will disappear, while the Lord protects His house.

answers: Tyre, Zidon, and the cities of the Philistines
Jerusalem, Hebron, and Bethlehem
Egypt, Babylon, and Nineveh
easy.explanation: The passage names Tyrus, Zidon, and several Philistine cities.
easy.q: Which cities are mentioned among those that will be judged?

answers: Horses and grain
Silver and fine gold
Weapons and shields
easy.explanation: Tyre heaped up silver as dust and fine gold as the mire of the streets.
easy.q: What did Tyre heap up in great amounts?

answers: The king of Ekron
The army of Tyre
The LORD
easy.explanation: The LORD promises to encamp around His house and protect it.
easy.q: Who says, “I will encamp about mine house”?

answers: They will remain forever
The city will be cast out and its power destroyed
They will be given to Zidon
medium.explanation: The LORD will cast Tyre out and smite her power in the sea.
medium.q: What will happen to Tyre’s wealth and stronghold?

answers: A fortified place of protection
A joyful song
A field of grain
medium.explanation: A strong hold is a fortified place built for defense.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “a strong hold” most nearly mean?

answers: It becomes stronger than before
It is cut off, though a remnant remains for God
It is transferred to Tyre
medium.explanation: The LORD says, “I will cut off the pride of the Philistines,” yet one who remains will be for God.
medium.q: What happens to the pride of the Philistines?

answers: Tyre trusts in wealth and fortification, while the house of Israel receives the LORD’s protection
Tyre is protected by the LORD, while Israel is abandoned
Both depend only on agriculture
challenge.explanation: Tyre’s wealth and defenses cannot save it, but the LORD encamps around His house.
challenge.q: What contrast is presented between Tyre and the house of Israel?

answers: The LORD’s action is only a distant possibility
The LORD is not involved in events
The LORD has seen the situation and is acting to protect His people
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the LORD’s direct awareness and immediate protective action.
challenge.q: What does the statement “for now have I seen with mine eyes” emphasize?

answers: It moves from the cities’ wealth and pride to their downfall and the LORD’s protection
It moves from a feast to the building of the temple
It moves from Israel’s victory to Israel’s exile
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with powerful cities and ends with their judgment and the protection of the LORD’s house.
challenge.q: How does the prophecy develop in verses 1–8?

paragraphs.idea: The prophecy describes the downfall of Tyre, Sidon, and the Philistine cities. Their wealth, fortifications, and pride will disappear, while the Lord protects His house.

paragraphs.title: The Humble King and Universal Peace
paragraphs.paragraph: Jerusalem is called to rejoice at the coming of a righteous and humble king riding upon a donkey. He will remove weapons of war, speak peace to the nations, and release prisoners of hope.

answers: The daughter of Zion and the daughter of Jerusalem
Tyre and Zidon
The sons of Greece
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem.”
easy.q: Who is commanded to rejoice and shout?

answers: A war horse
An ass and a colt, the foal of an ass
A chariot
easy.explanation: The King is described as riding upon an ass and a colt.
easy.q: What does the King ride upon?

answers: They will be increased
They will be sold to foreign nations
They will be cut off
easy.explanation: The chariot, horse, and battle bow will be cut off.
easy.q: What will happen to the weapons of war?

answers: The King will speak peace unto the heathen
The King will rule only Jerusalem
The King will give the weapons to Tyre
medium.explanation: After the weapons are removed, the prophecy says that the King will speak peace to the nations.
medium.q: What is the connection between removing weapons and the King’s rule?

answers: He brings or possesses deliverance
He builds a wall
He declares war
medium.explanation: “Having salvation” presents the King as one associated with deliverance and victory.
medium.q: In the phrase “having salvation,” what does the KJV wording suggest about the King?

answers: They will be sent into battle
They will be sent forth from the pit
They will be given fortified cities
medium.explanation: The LORD says, “I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.”
medium.q: What is promised to the prisoners in the pit where there is no water?

answers: He is lowly, yet His dominion reaches from sea to sea
He is wealthy and fortified, yet rules no one
He is cruel in battle, yet refuses peace
challenge.explanation: The King is humble and riding on a donkey, but His dominion extends to the ends of the earth.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the description of the King?

answers: The King brings peace, wide dominion, and release
Tyre gives Jerusalem its wealth
All the nations leave the land
challenge.explanation: The King’s coming brings salvation, peace, universal rule, and freedom for prisoners of hope.

answers: Jerusalem rejoices, the King comes, warfare ends, and prisoners are released
Tyre is destroyed, rebuilt, and sent to war
Israel fights, is defeated, and returns to exile
challenge.explanation: The passage proceeds from rejoicing to the King’s arrival, peace, and the release of prisoners.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in verses 9–12?

paragraphs.idea: Jerusalem is called to rejoice at the coming of a righteous and humble king riding upon a donkey. He will remove weapons of war, speak peace to the nations, and release prisoners of hope.

paragraphs.title: War against Greece and Divine Victory
paragraphs.paragraph: The LORD uses Judah and Ephraim as instruments of war and raises Zion against Greece. He appears, defends His people, and grants them victory.

answers: The sons of Tyre
The sons of Greece
The sons of Egypt
easy.explanation: The LORD raises the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece.
easy.q: Against whom are the sons of Zion raised?

answers: A shield
A bow
A crown
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim.”

answers: He defends them
He delivers them to their enemies
He hides them from the land
easy.explanation: The passage says, “The LORD of hosts shall defend them.”
easy.q: What does the LORD do for His people on that day?

answers: As weapons in the LORD’s hand
As prisoners in a pit
As fortified cities
medium.explanation: Judah is bent like a bow, and Ephraim fills the bow as part of the LORD’s battle.
medium.q: How are Judah and Ephraim portrayed together?

answers: A hidden object
A banner or signal raised for display
A broken weapon
medium.explanation: An ensign is a banner or visible sign lifted up.
medium.q: In the phrase “lifted up as an ensign,” what does “ensign” most nearly mean?

answers: It signals the LORD’s appearance and advance into battle
It announces the grape harvest
It is used to build the wall
medium.explanation: The LORD God blows the trumpet and goes with the whirlwinds of the south.
medium.q: What is the role of the trumpet in the description of battle?

answers: The value and honor of Israel in the LORD’s land
Israel’s weakness and scattering
That Israel is useful only for construction
challenge.explanation: Crown stones are precious and honored, so the image emphasizes Israel’s value.
challenge.q: What does the image of Israel as “the stones of a crown” communicate?

answers: The LORD appears as a warrior, defends them, and gives them power to overcome
The LORD withdraws, and the people win without help
The LORD disarms the people and gives them to their enemies
challenge.explanation: The LORD is seen over them, sends forth His arrow, blows the trumpet, and defends His people.
challenge.q: How do the LORD’s appearance and defense contribute to the people’s victory?

answers: From preparing weapons for battle to the LORD’s appearance, protection, and victory
From agricultural blessing to the building of cities
From releasing prisoners to imprisoning them again
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from Judah and Ephraim as weapons to the LORD’s direct intervention and Israel’s victory.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in verses 13–16?

paragraphs.idea: The LORD uses Judah and Ephraim as instruments of war and raises Zion against Greece. He appears, defends His people, and grants them victory.

paragraphs.title: Abundance, Beauty, and Joy
paragraphs.paragraph: The final verse praises the goodness and beauty of that day and describes an abundance of corn and new wine that brings joy to the young men and maids.

answers: His goodness and His beauty
The walls of Tyre
The weapons of war
easy.explanation: The verse asks, “For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty!”
easy.q: What is described as great in the final verse?

answers: Corn
Water alone
Silver
easy.explanation: The verse says, “corn shall make the young men cheerful.”
easy.q: What will make the young men cheerful?

answers: It will make them joyful
It will send them into battle
It will build them a stronghold
easy.explanation: New wine is described as bringing cheer and joy to the maids.
easy.q: What will new wine do for the maids?

answers: Both represent abundance and blessing in the land
Both are weapons of war
Both are signs of destruction
medium.explanation: Corn and new wine represent provision, prosperity, and joy.
medium.q: What relationship exists between corn and new wine in the verse?

answers: Fresh wine made from the produce of the vine
Refined silver
A weapon of war
medium.explanation: New wine refers to fresh wine or the fresh produce of the grape harvest.
medium.q: What does “new wine” mean in this verse?

answers: Corn strengthens the young men, and new wine brings joy to the maids
Corn weakens the people, and wine frightens them
Corn builds defenses, and wine prepares the army
medium.explanation: The verse connects corn with cheer among young men and new wine with joy among the maids.
medium.q: How does the verse describe the effect of the produce on society?

answers: It presents goodness, beauty, abundance, and joy after deliverance and victory
It returns only to the destruction of the cities
It cancels everything stated earlier
challenge.explanation: The final verse portrays the blessed result of the LORD’s saving work.
challenge.q: Why can this verse be viewed as a summary of the prophecy?

answers: The people’s abundant and joyful life
The construction of weapons
The increase of Tyre’s wealth
challenge.explanation: The verse focuses on goodness, beauty, food, and gladness.
challenge.q: Which aspect of restoration is emphasized most strongly?

answers: The blessing reaches different groups within the people and affects their daily lives
The blessing is intended only for kings
The verse concerns only the army
challenge.explanation: The verse names young men and maids to show that the blessing brings joy throughout the community.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from mentioning both young men and maids?

paragraphs.idea: The final verse praises the goodness and beauty of that day and describes an abundance of corn and new wine that brings joy to the young men and maids.
